project_type: Multi-system emulator. Rust core engine (crates/emulator-bridge) compiled to WASM for a web PWA and to native ARM64 for iOS via a UniFFI Swift facade. Phase 5 built the native libretro loader and the iOS pipeline (native/ios/); the only compiler for iOS is GitHub Actions on macos-latest and the only debugger is the on-screen HUD.
language: Rust (engine), C/C++ (libretro cores + switch-wrapper), Swift (iOS shell), Bash (build scripts), YAML (CI).
build_system: Cargo workspace pinned to Rust 1.92.0 (rust-toolchain.toml). iOS engine: `cargo build --profile ios --target aarch64-apple-ios --features native-core,uniffi-bindings` (custom [profile.ios] inherits release but sets panic=unwind, so artefacts land in target/aarch64-apple-ios/ios/, NOT .../release/). Web cores: scripts/build-core.sh with wasi-sdk into web/cores/. iOS cores: scripts/build-core.sh with Apple clang and the iphoneos SDK into native/ios/build/lib/.
test_framework: cargo test. 74 tests plain, 84 with --features native-core,uniffi-bindings. C++ wrapper harness: native/switch-wrapper/build.sh host (15 checks).
build_command: cargo check --profile ios --target aarch64-apple-ios --features native-core,uniffi-bindings (all this sandbox can do for iOS). On the macOS runner: native/ios/build-engine.sh then native/ios/package-ipa.sh.
verification_instructions: In this Linux sandbox: (1) cargo test -> 74 passing; (2) cargo test --features native-core,uniffi-bindings -> 84 passing (proves Rust untouched); (3) cargo check --profile ios --target aarch64-apple-ios --features native-core,uniffi-bindings -> clean; (4) swiftc -frontend -parse on native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift and native/ios/MetalCanvas.swift -> exit 0 (SPELL-CHECK ONLY: no iOS SDK here, so SwiftUI/UIKit and the generated UniFFI facade are not type-checked and the core table's types, the coreState Optional handling, List/ForEach identity and the extension routing must be reviewed by eye); (5) bash -n on scripts/build-core.sh, native/ios/build-engine.sh, native/ios/package-ipa.sh; (6) python3 yaml.safe_load on native/ios/project.yml and .github/workflows/ios.yml, python3 plistlib.load on native/ios/Info.plist; (7) `bash scripts/build-core.sh ios-names` -> the five canonical dylib filenames, runnable on Linux because it only prints the table; (8) TRACE THE FIVE CANONICAL DYLIB NAMES BY EYE across build-core.sh, build-engine.sh, project.yml, package-ipa.sh, ios.yml and ContinuumApp.swift; (9) confirm bare `build-core.sh fceumm|mgba|genesis_plus_gx|snes9x|all` still routes to the WASM path and nothing writes into web/. The macOS dylib builds, the .ipa build and the on-device launch of each system are verified ONLY by the orchestrator's CI run and device test afterward.
snapshot_or_generated_files: UniFFI Swift bindings are generated into native/ios/build/Generated/ (gitignored, never committed). The .xcodeproj is generated by xcodegen from native/ios/project.yml (gitignored). Core sources land in .work/ and web cores in web/cores/, both gitignored. No generated files are committed for this task.
setup_instructions: rustup toolchain comes from rust-toolchain.toml (1.92.0, targets wasm32-unknown-unknown and aarch64-apple-ios, already installed). Nothing else is needed for the verifiable gates; the iOS core builds cannot run here at all.
environment_constraints: No macOS, no Xcode, no iOS SDK. Network is open, which is how each upstream core's makefile was read during planning, but neither scripts/build-core.sh's iOS path nor native/ios/*.sh will run here: they refuse on a non-Darwin host by design. The wasi-sdk web path in build-core.sh must keep working untouched.
contribution_requirements: Do NOT touch web/. Do NOT modify crates/** (no Rust change is needed: NativeLibretroCore is core-agnostic and CoreRegistry already holds many declared cores). Do NOT push, open or modify a PR, or trigger CI; the orchestrator publishes. Commit locally on branch ps1-pcsx-rearmed. SESSION_HANDOFF.md must record the change. No em dashes in code, comments, strings or docs. Every failure path writes a distinct HUD string.
key_patterns:
THE BIGGEST TRAP: `scripts/build-core.sh <name>` already means 'build <name> as WASM for the web'. `fceumm`, `mgba`, `genesis_plus_gx`, `snes9x` and `all` are live, documented WASM invocations (web/cores/README.md, README.md, SESSION_HANDOFF.md, scripts/core-abi-test.mjs buildHint strings, .github/workflows/deploy.yml). The existing iOS path was added as `build-core.sh pcsx_rearmed`, which was safe only because pcsx_rearmed has no WASM case block. Making `build-core.sh fceumm` build an iOS dylib would BREAK THE WEB BUILD, so the iOS path must live in its own subcommand namespace (`ios <core>`, `ios-all`) dispatched before ensure_toolchain so wasi-sdk is never fetched and web/cores/ is never touched.

PER-CORE iOS BUILD GROUND TRUTH, read from each upstream makefile during planning (not assumed):
  fceumm          libretro/libretro-fceumm, Makefile.libretro at the repo root (the root Makefile is a one-line include of it). `platform=ios-arm64` sets CC='cc -arch arm64 -isysroot $(IOSSDK)', SHARED=-dynamiclib, -miphoneos-version-min=8.0, TARGET_NAME=fceumm and TARGET=fceumm_libretro_ios.dylib at the root. NOTE: the iOS block also forces WANT_32BPP := 1, so this core renders XRGB8888 rather than the RGB565 the WASM build uses; the declared pixel format is a pre-load hint only and SET_PIXEL_FORMAT during retro_load_game settles it.
  genesis_plus_gx libretro/Genesis-Plus-GX, Makefile.libretro at the repo root. `platform=ios-arm64` sets CC/CXX to 'cc|c++ -arch arm64 -isysroot $(IOSSDK)', SHARED=-dynamiclib (no --version-script on iOS), IOSSDK defaults from `xcrun -sdk iphoneos -show-sdk-path`, LIBS=-lm, TARGET_NAME=genesis_plus_gx and TARGET=genesis_plus_gx_libretro_ios.dylib at the root.
  snes9x          libretro/snes9x, the makefile is libretro/Makefile and it sets CORE_DIR := .., so make must run INSIDE the libretro subdirectory and TARGET lands there. `platform=ios-arm64` sets CC/CXX to arm64 with -isysroot, LD=$(CXX) so libc++ comes in, LTO=-flto, TARGET_NAME=snes9x and TARGET=snes9x_libretro_ios.dylib.
  mgba            libretro/mgba has NO makefile at all: the libretro core is a CMake target (BUILD_LIBRETRO=ON), which is also why the WASM path uses CMake for it (CMake generates version.c). So the iOS path configures CMake with CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME=iOS, CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 and CMAKE_OSX_SYSROOT=<iphoneos sdk>, builds the mgba_libretro STATIC archive (mgba_libretro.a, PREFIX is forced to empty and the SUFFIX is set explicitly by CMakeLists), and then links the dylib itself with `cc -arch arm64 -isysroot <sdk> -dynamiclib -Wl,-force_load <archive> -framework Foundation -lm`. -force_load is load-bearing: nothing in the link references retro_*, so without it the linker would pull no archive members in and emit an empty dylib. Two upstream details worth knowing: mgba's CMakeLists forces CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET to 10.6 inside its `if(APPLE)` block, which only lowers the objects' minimum OS and does not break the build, and it adds -flto to Release flags on Apple, so the archive holds bitcode that ld resolves at link time.
  pcsx_rearmed    libretro/pcsx_rearmed, Makefile.libretro at the root, already working: recursive submodules (lightrec, libchdr), `platform=ios-arm64` forces DYNAREC=0 (interpreter only), TARGET=pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib.
So four of the five canonical names are exactly what upstream emits and only mgba's is ours.

THE FIVE CANONICAL DYLIB NAMES, which must match byte for byte across six files (scripts/build-core.sh, native/ios/build-engine.sh, native/ios/project.yml, native/ios/package-ipa.sh, .github/workflows/ios.yml, native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift): fceumm_libretro_ios.dylib, mgba_libretro_ios.dylib, genesis_plus_gx_libretro_ios.dylib, snes9x_libretro_ios.dylib, pcsx_rearmed_libretro_ios.dylib.

EXTENSION TO CORE ROUTING, the one table both the Library row and the launch path consult: nes -> fceumm; sfc, smc -> snes9x; gba, gb, gbc -> mgba; sms, gg, md, gen -> genesis_plus_gx; cue, chd, pbp, iso -> pcsx_rearmed. importableExtensions is that key set plus bin; launchableExtensions is importable minus bin, because a .bin is a CD track that a cue sheet names and never a launch target.

ARCHITECTURAL INVARIANTS that must survive: import-and-copy into Documents with original filenames and no rename-on-collision ever (a .cue names its .bin tracks literally), collision replaces, per-file do/catch; no security-scoped URLs on the launch path; engine.coreState is the single source of truth with no cached Bool; ensureCoreLoaded(coreId:) is called AFTER stopSession() because stop() unloads the core under the Drop retention policy; one MTLDevice created by Rust/wgpu and read back by Swift; the picker stays [UTType.item] + asCopy: true + allowsMultipleSelection with its strongly retained delegate and all four @objc callbacks.
